bases.note: No absolute address is hardcoded anywhere.

guest_image_base.source: /proc/<pid>/maps: the anonymous, read-only, offset-0 region (the recompiled image)

host_module_base.note: not used for game state; host symbols are unrelated to fighter state

candidates.note: The camera manager singleton is the anonymous pointer at BossManager::instance_ + 8 (0x52b7f00). app::camera::get_dead_area reads it with adrp 0x52b7000 / ldr [x8,#0xf00]; no CameraManager dynsym exists.
app::sv_information::stage_id (0x227ebb0) reads adrp 0x5329000 / ldr [x8,#0x9d8] = this global, then ldr x8,[x8], then ldr w9,[x8,#0x17c]; 0xffffffff means no stage.

chain.note: Every offset below was read out of the game's own lua_bind accessor with aarch64-linux-gnu-objdump, not guessed.

control_module.module + 0x110: u64 -> input struct (live: module+0x20; the getters dereference this)
control_module.module + 0x120: u32 direction flag; nonzero negates stick_x and sub_stick_x
control_module.note: The offsets above are the resolved values on this build. gamestate.py reads the vtable, follows each virtual getter and decodes the tiny loader at run time, so a changed build resolves itself.

work_module.note: get_int/set_int dispatch through the work vtable +0x98; get_float through +0x58. Instance ints are kind 0.

camera_chain.note: app::camera::get_dead_area and sv_camera_manager::dead_range read this exact chain.
steps: left, right, top, bottom = f32x4 at manager + 0xC30

evidence.note: disassembly that proves each struct offset

PostureModule__pos_x_impl.asm: ldr x0,[x0,#56]; ldr x8,[x0]; ldr x8,[x8,#96]; blr x8; ldr s0,[x0]

posture_vtable_12_target.conclusion: position vector starts at PostureModule+0x30 (x,y,z float32)

StatusModule__situation_kind_impl.conclusion: situation_kind = u32 at StatusModule+0xDC; 0 = on ground

DamageModule__damage_impl.getter: 0x3ff9f0: ldr x8,[x0,#24]; ldr s0,[x8, x1*0x1c0]; ret

WorkModule__get_int_impl.conclusion: work int array = *(*(*(WorkModule+0x18)) + 0x20), stride 8, index = id & 0xffffff

WorkModule__is_enable_transition_term_im.asm: ldr x9,[x0,#40]; and w8,w1,#0xffffff; ldrb w10,[x9,x8]; ...
WorkModule__is_enable_transition_term_im.conclusion: terms = *(WorkModule+0x28); enabled = 0 if (b&0x38) else ((b>>2)&1) if (b&2) else (b&1)

FighterInformation__kind_impl.conclusion: kind = u8 at record+0x30, minus 1. Live: P0 record+0x30=1 -> Mario kind 0; P1=2 -> DK kind 1.

FighterInformation__stock_impl.conclusion: stock = u8 at record+0xD8. In the debug rule (0 stocks) it reads 0; a nonzero-stock rule is not yet exercised.

ControlModule__get_sub_stick_x_impl.conclusion: C-stick x is vtable+0x200 (512); the game calls the sub stick the C stick

concrete_control_getters.note: Resolved live from the module vtable (0x7104f84de0 on the 13.0.4 build); guest offsets are target - guest_base.
concrete_control_getters.get_stick_x: 0x3f84a0: ldr x9,[x0,#0x110]; ldr s0,[x9,#0x10]; ldr w8,[x0,#0x120]; cmp w8,#0; fneg s1,s0; fcsel s0,s0,s1,eq; ret
concrete_control_getters.get_sub_stick_x: 0x3f85c0: ldr x9,[x0,#0x110]; ldr s0,[x9,#0x40]; ldr w8,[x0,#0x120]; cmp w8,#0; fneg s1,s0; fcsel s0,s0,s1,eq; ret
concrete_control_getters.conclusion: gamestate.py follows the vtable, reads the loader bytes, decodes the two LDRs and uses the offsets; the constants above are only the fallback.

ControlModule__check_button_trigger_impl.wrapper: ldr x0,[x0,#72]; ldr x8,[x0]; ldr x2,[x8,#592]; br x2  -> vtable+0x250
ControlModule__check_button_trigger_impl.concrete: 0x3f8670: blr [vtable+0x220] (get_trigger); adrp x8,0x4538000; add x8,x8,#0xfec; ldr w8,[x8,w19,sxtw #2]; tst w8,w0; cset w0,ne
ControlModule__check_button_trigger_impl.conclusion: The game's own button-id -> mask table proves the 12 canonical bits used by schema.BUTTON_BITS.

StageManager__stage_id.asm: adrp x8,0x5329000; ldr x8,[x8,#0x9d8]; cbz x8,ret -1; ldr x8,[x8]; ldr w9,[x8,#0x17c]; cmn w9,#1; ...
StageManager__stage_id.conclusion: stage_id = u32 at *(*(StageManager::instance_)) + 0x17C; 0xffffffff = no stage. Live: 0 during a fight (this is the select-screen information copy).
StageManager__stage_id.fallback: match block guest offset 0x52c41b0 (runtime/debug_mode.c GA(0x71052c41b0)), stage id at +0x420; the debug hook prints this same value at match start. Live: 0x125 = 293 on Final Destination.

FighterInformation__stock_count_impl.conclusion: stock = u32 at record+0xD8 (216), not u8; stored as int32 in the shared block

camera__get_dead_area.conclusion: two derefs then float32x4 at manager+0xC30 = (left, right, top, bottom)

KineticModule__get_sum_speed_x_impl.conclusion: KineticModule = *(accessor+0x68); vtable[24] returns vx, vtable[25] returns vy (requires calling guest code; reader derives velocity from position instead)

entry_id.note: player slot 0..1; entries 0 and 1 are the two players

kind.note: Live: P0 = 0 (Mario), P1 = 1 (Donkey Kong). The record is static but the kind never changes during a match.

stock.note: The game's own FighterInformation__stock_count accessor loads a 32-bit word. The debug rule on this save is 0 stocks, so the live value is 0; the offset/width are proven by the accessor.

is_cpu.note: 0 = human, 1 = CPU. Published in the fighter slot now (v7); it is no longer used to reorder the slots.

is_on_rebirth.note: The game's FighterInformation__is_on_rebirth accessor (0x20c9f10: ldrb [x8,#908]). 1 while the fighter waits on the revival platform.

is_enable_cancel.note: CancelModule::is_enable_cancel. Nonzero while the current action can be cancelled.

shield.address: derived from action_state in a GUARD status
shield.note: v1: 1 while the status kind is the held-guard kind. Live 60 Hz CPU match: shield 0->1 at status 10 and back to 0 at 11/12/34 (29 and 27 transitions); status kind 10 is the exact guard kind. shield_size has no verified source yet and is published as 0.0.

hitstun.note: 1 while the fighter is in a damage reaction (54..62, 476..479, 505..511), else 0. Derived from the same status kind the game's StatusModule exposes.

buttons.note: Raw ControlModule button bitmask, resolved through the get_button virtual getter at vtable+0x238. Decoded into schema.BUTTON_ORDER (A B X Y L R ZL ZR PLUS MINUS DPAD_L DPAD_R).

stick_x.note: get_stick_x at vtable+0x178; the concrete loader also reads module+0x120 and applies fneg+fcsel. Clamped to [-1,1].

stick_y.note: get_stick_y at vtable+0x188; no sign flip.

cstick_x.note: get_sub_stick_x at vtable+0x200 (the game calls the C stick the sub stick). Same sign flip as stick_x.

trigger.note: The getter loads a word; gamestate accepts either a 0..0xffff fixed-point value or a float bit pattern and publishes [0,1].

stage_id.note: Header field. app::sv_information::stage_id reads the StageManager chain; 0xffffffff = no stage. That field is 0 in-match on this build, so the match block's in-match stage id (the value the debug hook prints) is used as the fallback. Live with stage=end: 0x3 = Final Destination; source is recorded in GameState.last_stage_source.

game_frame.note: Monotonic reader frame index (not yet the game's internal frame counter). Header field.

flags.note: bit 0 = stage_id was read this frame; bit 1 = the ControlModule virtual getters were resolved.

y.note: component 1; 0.01 on the floor, >0 jumping, <0 falling off the stage

damage.note: index 0. Verified against the HUD: memory 36.347 = screen 36.3%

facing.note: +1 / -1; flips exactly when the character turns around

action_state.note: status kind: 0 wait, 1 walk, 6 dash, 11 jump squat, 12 jump, 18 fall, 54 damage, 73 cliff catch, 263 KO, 476 tumble

action_frame.note: increments within an action and resets when the status changes

on_ground.note: situation_kind == 0. Observed 0 on the floor, 2 on the revival platform, 5 while falling to a KO

is_actionable.address: derived: count of enabled bytes in u64(WorkModule + 0x28)[0..255] >= 4
is_actionable.note: Uses the game's own transition-term table (the same bytes is_enable_transition_term reads). Live counts: WAIT ~49, dash ~44, jump ~32, cliff ~12, hitstun 2, tumble/KO 0. A fallback action-state table is kept only for the rare frame where the term table is unreadable.

jumps_left.note: index 6 = jump_count_max, index 4 = jump_count. Live: Mario 2 on the ground, 1 after one jump / on a cliff; DK 1. This replaced the old guess that no work int behaved like a jump counter.

vx.note: The engine getter (KineticModule vtable[24]) needs a guest call; the position delta is an exact enough estimate at 60 Hz and is what the reader publishes.

dist_to_blast.address: derived: min(x-left, right-x, y-bottom, top-y) with the live camera bounds
dist_to_blast.note: Bounds come from the camera manager, not a table. Live: (-240,240,180,-140), (-280,280,180,-140), (-250,170,185,-65). Clamped to >= 0.

dx.note: SELF sees the opponent's offset; the OPPONENT row is the negation.

facing_rel.note: +1 = opponent is in front, -1 = behind, 0 = unknown/degenerate. Computed per row from that row's own facing.

match_state.address: derived from ready_go + fighter-entry allocation in gamestate.py
match_state.note: 0=MENU (entry 0/1 freed and no recent fight), 1=IN_MATCH (ready_go=1), 2=RESULTS (entries still allocated, or within 8 s of ready_go dropping). The old 'was in a fight' test wrongly reported RESULTS forever at the main menu.

tried: read as u32 now (the game's accessor loads w0)
stock_nonzero.note: The address/width are proven by FighterInformation__stock_count (ldr w0,[x8,#216]). The value is 0 because the debug match runs the saved 0-stock rule. Run a stock match to confirm the unit.

tried: searched main.elf for inline pointers to the 485 FIGHTER_STATUS_KIND_* strings: none
searched .rela.dyn and .rela.plt for addends equal to those string vaddrs: none (they are referenced only by PC-relative code)
status_kind_names.note: ACTION_STATE_NAMES in schema.py is the common Smash status-kind enum. The values used by the verifier (0,1,6,11,12,18,54,73,263,476) are confirmed live; character-specific specials may be off by a few names.

verification.method: screenshot of the game window (xwd) compared against a probe run in the same second; widget text read headlessly from the Tk verifier

observations: y = -145 while falling to a KO
Mario 1 after one jump / while on a cliff

actionable_check.result: matches the game's own transition-term accessor

blast_check.method: two derefs from BossManager::instance_ + 8, f32x4 at manager+0xC30

input_check.method: click the HUD, then click the game (a real FocusOut/FocusIn), then xdotool key z
input_check.result: the menu advanced and a match started. xdotool windowfocus alone sets X input focus but leaves SDL_GetKeyboardFocus() NULL, so GetForegroundWindow() returns NULL and nnhid.c ignores GetAsyncKeyState. live.sh performs the click round-trip.

notes: The FighterInformation object is embedded at entry+0xF0; the game's accessors take that address and start with ldr x8,[x0,#8]. u64(entry+0xF8) is therefore the information record, not a separate object.
Guest image maps at 0x71_00000000 (10 hex digits); heap allocations are at 0x7100_xxxxxxxx (12 digits). A naive range check confuses the two.
run.py strips SSBU_* environment variables; pass them with --env, and input sequences with --seq.

SSBU_DEBUG_MATCH applies the saved rules. With the saved 0-stock rule a KO ends the match and the game immediately restarts it (the debug hook re-applies the setup), so matches cycle every ~10-15 s. stock= is only applied when the panel state's rule kind is already 1, which it is not on this save.
vx/vy are derived from position deltas, not read from the engine (the KineticModule getter would need a guest call).
is_actionable uses the game's own transition-term table; the old ACTIONABLE_TABLE is only a fallback for an unreadable term table.

The keyboard only reaches the game while the SDL window has the X11 input focus. xdotool windowactivate (EWMH) silently fails under mutter; xdotool windowfocus works. tools/mem/live.sh installs a focus keeper for this.

A torn-down fighter entry can hold a non-null object pointer with status 0x7fffffff; gamestate.py rejects rows with an out-of-range status or non-finite coordinates so the verifier does not flash red during a results transition.
v7 slots are fixed in player order (slot 0 = entry 0/P1, slot 1 = entry 1/P2). The old human-first reorder is gone; use is_cpu to tell them apart.

The ControlModule getters are virtual. gamestate.py resolves the concrete function from the live vtable, decodes its ldr/ldrb instructions and uses those offsets; the documented constants are the fallback when a module is being torn down.
